problem: What is the value of $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{t+1} \\ 1-{t}^{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡t\end{aligned}]$ at $t=0?$
worked_solution:
To evaluate, we substitute $t=0$ into the function, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(0) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{(0)+1} \\ 1-(0)^{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(0)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{1} \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the value of $f(t)$ at $t=0$ is $[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}].$
